summary: Iteration 15. I read RideAccessibilityService.kt after the follow-up edits and found no compile errors. There is no kotlinc here, so this is a read-through, not a build. (1) offerText returns Pair<String,String> and the caller destructures it correctly. priceText is a local var with no lambda capture, so the smart cast makes Pair(priceText, all) type-check as Pair<String,String>. Sequence.count() is valid. (2) retryIfStillShown runs inside the postDelayed Runnable lambda. break/continue inside its for loop are legal, and comparing Double? to Double with == is valid. (3) tap() uses maxOf(0f, exactCenterX/Y()) and returns a Boolean from the try/catch expression. I updated the Python simulation to the new pair-returning offerText and added tap clamp and retry same-price ports: 11/11 pass with -n0. The requested edge case passes: the card has R$ 9,60 and 1 km, and an ancestor has 2+ km plus a background R$ 15,00; price is now 9.60. Notes 1, 2 and 4 from iteration 14 are resolved for price, tap safety and retry. A remaining km leak was found (see action_items). Regression checks: GET /api/ returns 200 {"message":"RapidoChecker API"}, and the login screen renders on a 390x844 mobile viewport with the logo, CPF input and Entrar button. I did not test admin login, as requested.
action_items: (Low/Medium) Remaining km leak in offerText. The price is now correct, but the km text still comes from the first scope at or above the price scope that has 2+ km. If the card shows only 1 km and an ancestor also holds the background list's km values, those values get mixed in. Example from test_edge_km_from_ancestor_mixes_background_km: the background has 3 km and 5 km, and the card has R$ 9,60 and 2,76 km. The result is pickup=3, trip=5 and R$/km=1.92 instead of pickup=0, trip=2.76 and R$/km=3.48. This could wrongly reject a good offer. Suggested fix: while climbing for km, stop once the scope has more price matches than the price scope (priceRe.findAll(all).count() > priceCount), then use kmFallback. This only matters if Moove's pop-up shows a single km, which the screenshot does not: it shows 2 km in the same card.

(Info) retryIfStillShown only checks the price. A different offer with the same price appearing within 700ms would also be tapped, which is unlikely and acceptable. You could also compare tripKm and pickupKm, which are already parsed, for a stricter match.
(Info, unchanged) The null-package TYPE_WINDOWS_CHANGED branch is best effort because serviceInfo.packageNames filters out those events. The pop-up is still caught through its own events.
critical_code_review_comments: Iteration 14 note 1, background price leak: RESOLVED. The price comes from the smallest scope that has a price. The new km leak is described in action_items.
Iteration 14 note 2, tap safety: RESOLVED. x and y are clamped to >= 0, an empty rect returns false, and Path, StrokeDescription and dispatchGesture are wrapped in try/catch returning false.

Iteration 14 note 4, retry taps any 'Aceitar' button: RESOLVED. It now taps only if the same price is still shown, and does nothing when the pop-up is gone or the price differs. The simulation covers all three cases.
In acceptIfMatches, the destructuring val (priceText, kmText) = offerText(...) is valid. The price regex is applied to priceText and the km regex to kmText, as intended.
ride_filter_accessibility.xml is unchanged and valid: typeWindowsChanged, canPerformGestures=true and flagRetrieveInteractiveWindows are present.
